editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher article, review and press-release text is never copied; explained in Swoon'd's own words with a link to the original. No product reviews, ratings or before/after imagery are used or redistributed.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: She can follow a conversation about someone's routine, a sunscreen or an ingredient, name what is being discussed, ask a real question about it, and say 'okay, I see why you love this' without faking expertise, giving skin advice or judging anyone's skin, tone or budget.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Original vector illustrations and procedural diagrams only (license original-swoond); no photos of skin or faces, no model likeness, no stock skin-condition images, no before/after, no real product photography.
No brand logos or trade dress in art; brand names as text facts in dated live cards only; invented brand names in examples.
No embedded creator or brand video; deep-link to official pages.
Never copy publisher, review or press-release text; paraphrase and link.
Curated regulator facts with source links and dates; UV index from public providers (licence to confirm); no review, rating or price data; no scraping of retailers or review sites.
Creator and dermatologist names as sourced facts only; no likeness, endorsement implication or fabricated quotes; no content targeting an individual.

Health-adjacent: qualified dermatology/pharmacy review is required before any unit ships; no skin photos, face scans or skin analysis; `skin-type` and `concern` (contract 1.3) are optional, on-device flavor tokens only (no medical conditions), never sent to analytics, Unity telemetry or notifications, hidden in discreet mode, and need product-owner approval before use (OPEN_QUESTIONS P-35).

safetyConstraints: Never diagnose: no lesson names a skin condition as something a person has; no symptom checker.

Never give medical advice or treatment: acne, rosacea, eczema, pregnancy or breastfeeding, prescription retinoids, allergies, reactions and any new or changing spot route to 'ask a dermatologist or pharmacist'.
No personal product or routine recommendations and no dosing or strength instructions; strengths on labels are facts, not targets.
No before/after claims or imagery, no retouched faces, no outcome promises.
Patch-test framing: a cautious habit that lowers but does not remove risk; stop and ask a pharmacist if a reaction occurs.
Body-, age-, gender- and skin-tone inclusive, never shaming; no 'flawless', 'problem skin' or aging-is-bad language.
No brand shilling: no brand is ranked, recommended or disparaged; no affiliate content.
No fear-mongering, no miracle claims; 'toxic' and 'chemical-free' claims are examined, not endorsed.
Every unit requires review by a licensed dermatologist or pharmacist before release (docs/courses/skincare/SAFETY_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md).
Never encourage the learner to fake expertise or to comment on the person's skin.
